description.narrative:
The proposed project aims to provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to populations affected by Tropical Cyclone Chido, which devastated Mecufi District, Cabo Delgado Province, on December 15, 2024. The category 4 cyclone brought catastrophic winds of up to 180 km/h and gusts of up to 220 km/h, severely impacting Mecufi, Chiure, Namuno, Montepuez, Metuge, Macomia, Muidumbe, and Pemba in Cabo Delgado. As of December 20, 2024, the cyclone has resulted in 120 deaths, affecting 329,565 people, including 216,930 in Cabo Delgado. A total of 65,293 families have been impacted, leading to significant humanitarian needs. The cyclone has caused widespread destruction in: • Shelter: 13,343 homes partially destroyed, 39,133 homes destroyed, 1,349 people sheltering in temporary accommodation in Pemba, and 500 families (mostly women and children) in evacuation centers. These families require emergency shelter, non-food items, and support to recover from the disaster. • Health: Nearly 900 injuries reported by theNational Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD), including 740 in Cabo Delgado. Furthermore, 52 health facilities have been affected, which may impact access to healthcare. Medical care, health facility support, and access to healthcare are essential to address the health needs ofthe affected population. • Education: 250 schools affected, 1,126 classrooms destroyed, and 109,793 students and 1,556 teachers affected. The rehabilitation of school infrastructure and support for access to education are crucial to minimize the disruption to education. • WASH: compromised and damaged infrastructure poses an increased risk of waterborne diseases. Addressing WASH needs is essential to prevent the spread of diseases. • Food security and livelihoods: damage to agriculture/fisheries and livelihoods has immediate and longer-term effects on the community. According to INGD Cyclone Chido preliminary information on 20th of December 2024, more that 10000 small hold farmers whose livelihoods weredisrupted creating gaps in food availability and basic needs. • Protection: heightened risks of gender-based violence, child exploitation, and abuse due to displacement and shelter damage listed above. Support for evacuation centers and protection services is critical to address these concerns. According to WFP, Humanitarian food distributions to a total of 23000 people began on 17 December and concluded on the 20th of December 2024 in Pemba, Mecufi, Metuge and Chiure, through the Joint Response Plan by WFP, IOM and UNICEF. The situation in the region is complex, with ongoing displacement due to the terrorist violence since 2017 (armed conflict) and the post-election political instability, the Cyclone Chido exacerbated ongoing needs in those affected districts. The current response in country by the Mozambique government, UN Agencies and other NGOs reflectsthe magnitude and scale of the crisis, although a gap of over $10 million is reported. Major gaps are noticed in the fields of gender and protectionas well as the capacity of affected communities to address their diverse needs according to their own prioritization, therefore our Cyclone response will focus on these areas to cover the gaps in the districts of Chiure and Montepuez, where we areassisting Internal Displaced People (IDPs) and host communities responding to the El Niño related drought. The intervention proposed addresses urgent humanitarian needs based on government assessments in coordination with United Nations agencies and local authorities in the hardest-hit areas of Mecufi and Chiure districts. Oxfam will work together with a long-standing local partner (ADEL CD) in Chiure and Montepuez, where the partner already has a base and accumulated experiences targeting the critical unmetneeds of the most vulnerable with funding of CHAF. Specific Activities will be as follows (i) Voucher/Cash Based Programming (1,550 individuals/310 families): Support the most vulnerable families with vouchers/ cash for emergency and lifesaving basic needs for example food, family kits (household utensils, blankets, hygiene materials and clothes) to the most vulnerable households that lost their possessions. (ii) Gender and Protection (5,000 women and girls in fertility age): Distribute dignity kits to women and girls of sexual and reproductive age, which will include IEC material to help them address, report and seek support for protection and risks of gender-basedviolence gender. Gender equality will be incorporated into all activities, adhering to Oxfam’s Gender in Emergencies guidelines. Ananalysis and monitoring of gender inequalities will be carried out to inform and target project needs and ensure that interventionsare inclusive and sensitive to the specific needs of women and girls.
Oxfam willmaintain frequent communication with local government authorities and clusters led by the United Nations and with the entire humanitarian community to ensure a coordinated and complementary response, encouraging the exchange and sharing of informationandchallenges, avoiding overlaps and increasing reach and depthto the most vulnerable populations affected by the cyclone. Oxfam will work in coordination with organizations with a strong presence in Cabo Delgado, namely CARE International, Save the Children, Plan International, Agha Khan Foundation, Doctors Without Borders,INSO (for monitoring, analysis and management of security aspects), to expand and strengthen its response capacity. Oxfam's protection activities will focus on raising awareness about protection risks and providing affected populations, especially women and girls, with information on available services and how to access support safely. The response will include voucher/cash-for-protection initiatives, referrals to specialized services,psychological first aid, and inclusive, culturally sensitive approaches to enhance dignity and resilience.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
